open_items: ECB has flapped three times in under 24 hours, each with a distinct failure shape, after weeks of clean history: (1) cycle 535 (2026-09-07T18:01:22Z) whole-provider HTTP 503 outage, every check failing, resolved by cycle 536; (2) cycle 539 (2026-09-08T02:01:22Z) gateway-data 504 + direct-json ReadTimeout, resolved by cycle 540; (3) cycle 542 (2026-09-08T08:01:22Z) gateway-data network/transport error ("provider unreachable") + direct-metadata ReadTimeout, resolved by cycle 543. No two episodes share the same failing-check combination. Each self-resolved within one cycle; confirmed healthy through cycle 544 with a live recheck (direct dataflow listing, HTTP 200 in 1.2s) and no other endpoint moved in any of these cycles, ruling out a routine-side network problem. Gateway-side checks could not be independently rechecked live (no directly reachable deployed gateway instance from this session). Distinct from the cycle 199 ECB metadata-only 503, the contract-only 504 flaps at cycles 182-183 and 283-286, and the old HTTP 406 Accept-header issue fixed before cycle 44. Watch closely for a fourth occurrence; three episodes in under a day is a rate change worth escalating for real investigation if it continues.

ILO gateway-metadata-only 403 flap (new shape): first occurrence, cycle 526 (gateway metadata 403 Forbidden on dataflow listing, 2 attempts; gateway data, direct metadata, direct data, direct json all passed same cycle; no contract rows affected). Preceding 24 cycles (503-525) all healthy. Resolved by cycle 527, confirmed still healthy through cycle 544. Distinct from the cycle 268-269 gateway_issue episode (same metadata-only shape but HTTP 500, not 403) and from the broader both-metadata-and-data or blanket-403 episodes. Watch for a second occurrence of this specific shape.

ILO contract-only blanket 403 (new shape): second occurrence, started cycle 490, resolved by cycle 493 at the latest (exact recovery cycle within 491-492 not observable, since /api/contracts exposes only current state plus the latest single-cycle diff). All references:* assertions back to ok (contentconstraint reads ignored, as expected) at cycle 493, basic checks stayed ok throughout. First occurrence was cycle 418, resolved by the next cycle. This second occurrence ran longer (roughly 2-4 hours / 1-3 cycles) but still far short of the ninth provider_down episode's ~24h standing block. Watch for a third occurrence.

ILO blanket-403 provider_down episode: eleventh occurrence, started cycle 442, resolved by cycle 443 (one cycle), confirmed still healthy (basic checks) through cycle 544. Matches the usual one-to-two-cycle resolution pattern (244, 251, 260, 264, 272, 281, 321, 382, 412); only the ninth occurrence (cycles 396-411) ran long, escalating to a standing block at the ~24h/12-cycle mark. No cause has ever been confirmed for any occurrence; ILO gives no public status signal. Watch for a twelfth occurrence.

IMF provider_down flap: first occurrence, cycle 419 (gateway metadata 503, gateway data 503, direct metadata 503, direct data ReadTimeout, all at once), resolved by cycle 420. Confirmed with a live recheck at 2026-08-29T06:44Z (direct metadata HTTP 200). Distinct from the cycle 161 references:* 401 contract flap below. Watch for a second occurrence; none through cycle 544.

ESTAT list_dataflows timeout pattern: twenty-eighth occurrence cycle 505, confirmed resolved by cycle 506 (one cycle, as usual), stable healthy through cycle 544. Prior occurrence was cycle 503, resolved by cycle 504. Consistent with the long-running one-cycle-flap pattern (the gateway's own 60s call deadline firing under a slow response), not a new bug. Standing recommendation (raise deadline, stream listing, or cache parsed result in monitor/checks_gateway.py) remains open as a code-change-scope fix, not actioned by this read-only routine. Watch for a twenty-ninth occurrence.

ILO gateway_issue, both gateway metadata and gateway data HTTP 403 together, direct healthy: first occurrence of this exact combination, cycle 384, resolved by cycle 385. Distinct from the gateway-data-only flap (cycles 322, 370, metadata still passing) and from the gateway-metadata-500 episode (cycles 268-269, HTTP 500 not 403, data still passing). No second occurrence through cycle 544 outside of the cycle 454 blanket episode (see above, a different and broader shape). Watch for a second occurrence of this specific shape.

ABS gateway metadata empty-error-body flap: thirteenth occurrence, cycle 539 (gateway metadata: Error: with empty body; gateway data, direct metadata, direct data, direct json all passed same cycle), resolved by cycle 540, confirmed still healthy through cycle 544. Prior occurrence was cycle 527, resolved by 528. All thirteen occurrences have now resolved within one cycle. Empty error message itself still worth fixing under code-change scope (GatewayError/next_step in monitor/checks_gateway.py).

ILO gateway-data-only 403 flap (standalone): two occurrences on record, cycle 370 (resolved by 371) and cycle 322 (tail end of the cycle 321 blanket-403 episode). Both resolved within one to two cycles. No new occurrence through cycle 544 of this specific standalone shape (the cycle 384, 396-411, and 442 episodes are the broader both-metadata-and-data or blanket shapes, see above). Watch for a third occurrence of this standalone data-only shape.

SBS gateway DNS resolution flap: first occurrence, cycle 366 (`Temporary failure in name resolution` on gateway metadata, gateway data probe timed out), resolved by cycle 367. No second occurrence through cycle 544. Isolated to SBS; same failure shape previously seen for FBOS at cycle 50 (treated as infrastructure, not provider-down). Watch for a second occurrence; escalate if it recurs.

UNICEF HTTP 429 flap: ninth occurrence cycle 514 (direct data HTTP 429 only, gateway data and both metadata checks ok, unlike the eighth occurrence where gateway data and direct json also failed). Confirmed resolved by cycle 515, stable healthy through cycle 544. Live recheck at 2026-09-06T06:44Z: direct data HTTP 200. Prior occurrences cycle 126, 178, 262, 305, 346, 430, all resolved within one cycle, matching this one. Watch for a tenth occurrence.

ABS and ESTAT gateway_issue coincided in the same cycle twice now (cycle 319 and cycle 389, both resolved within one cycle). No third same-cycle occurrence through cycle 544 (cycles 526-527 had ABS and ILO gateway_issue in adjacent but different cycles, not the same cycle, and not paired with ESTAT). Watch for a third same-cycle ABS/ESTAT occurrence with matching failure text.

OECD gateway_issue 403 Forbidden episode (cycles 290-292, gateway list_dataflows and gateway data probe both HTTP 403, direct path healthy throughout): resolved by cycle 293. No new occurrence through cycle 544. Watch for a second occurrence; escalate for real if a future episode again spans more than one cycle.

ILO direct-path 403 flap (basic checks): tenth occurrence cycle 286, resolved by cycle 287 (one cycle, as usual), clean since (superseded by the blanket 403 pattern, a different and more severe pattern -- see above). Prior occurrences cycle 32, 94, 159, 166, 202, 238, 244, 249, 267. Watch for an eleventh occurrence of this specific direct-only shape.

ILO references:contentconstraint broken (500) at cycle 274 resolved by cycle 275 (reads `ignored`, not `broken`, in the current cycle's contract rows). Second occurrence overall of this assertion flapping (first was a same-cycle blip at cycle 199). Cycle 490's contentconstraint 403 was part of the contract-only blanket-403 shape above, not this 500-specific flap; still reads ignored at cycle 544. Watch for a third occurrence of the 500-specific flap.

ILO gateway_issue episode (cycles 268-269, gateway metadata HTTP 500 on list_dataflows, direct healthy throughout): resolved by cycle 270. No new occurrence through cycle 544. Distinct pattern from the cycle 322, 370, 384, and 396-411/442 gateway data/metadata 403 episodes (see above): different HTTP status (500 vs 403). Watch separately.

ECB contract-probe 504 flap (second pattern): constraint:availableconstraint (504 -> 404) and references:none (504 -> 200) both showed a was/now change in /api/contracts between cycle 283 and 286, verdict stayed ok throughout. No further changes list entries on these assertions through cycle 544. Not the same assertions as the cycles 182-183 references:* 504 flap (that watch item is separate, still clean). Watch for recurrence on these two assertions specifically.
ABS contract 503 flap: dialect:sdmx3 and errors:missing_artefact both returned 503 at cycle 234 only, resolved by cycle 235. No new occurrence through cycle 544. Watch for a second occurrence.

ECB metadata 503 (provider_down): occurred cycle 199 only, resolved by cycle 200. No new occurrence through cycle 544 outside of the three-episode cluster above (different shapes -- not this metadata-only pattern). Watch for a second occurrence of this specific shape.
ABS gateway metadata 502 Bad Gateway flap: occurred cycle 198 only, resolved by cycle 199. No new occurrence through cycle 544. Watch for recurrence. Distinct from the empty-error-body flap above.
UNICEF direct-path HTTP 404 'no data found' flap: occurred cycle 197 only, resolved by cycle 198. No new occurrence through cycle 544. Watch for a second occurrence.
STATSNZ auth:listing capability_appeared, first seen cycle 60, still present at cycle 544: listing served without credentials. Still open, not re-reported since no new change.

Content-Type parameter order (charset vs version) on structure responses varies between requests. Cosmetic, verdict stays ok. Expected to keep flapping across multiple endpoints; do not re-report unless the verdict itself changes. No change at cycle 544.
IMF references:* 401 flap: first and only occurrence, cycle 161, resolved by cycle 162. No new occurrence through cycle 544. Watch for a second occurrence.

ECB references:* 504 flap (cycles 182-183 pattern): first occurrence, cycles 182-183, resolved by cycle 184. No new occurrence through cycle 544 (the three-episode cluster above involves different assertions/checks). Watch for a second occurrence of this specific pattern.
